svg.title: Retrieval decides what can be found. The reranker only orders it.
svg.desc: The full issue text, on the same source snapshot and with no patch, hints, target files or target blocks, goes to one of the routes. BM25: a BM25 index over tree-sitter chunks, top 100 by lexical score, K 100, coverage 63.78%. Model-planned grep: Sonnet 4.6 in one call plans up to six regex or glob actions, rg runs them locally with match caps per file, the smallest code chunk around each match is taken, and they are merged round-robin and deduplicated to at most 100; a mean of 17.47 chunks, coverage 75.83%. Dense and hybrid: a CodeRankEmbed query vector, then FAISS top 100, or with BM25 through RRF top 100; K 100, coverage 71.98% and 75.28%. A route's pool holds code chunks of up to 3,000 characters each; BM25 and grep use no embeddings. A replaceable reranker orders it: Qwen3-Reranker, 4B on every route and 0.6B on BM25 and grep only, scoring query-code pairs on a local H100; or Jev 1.13 Decisions, one four-level relevance question per chunk, ten per request, with Python sorting the scores and keeping failed batches in order. The top five results are compared as complete paths on Recall@5, latency and cost. Coverage is the ceiling: a reranker cannot recover code that never entered the pool.
svg.text: Retrieval decides what can be found. The reranker only orders it.
FAISS top 100, or + BM25 with RRF top 100
Coverage is the ceiling: a reranker cannot recover code that never entered the pool.
All four routes use base-aligned labels on the same 100 CodeNib Base issues. Each route's candidate pool is frozen and shared by its rerankers.
